findings.issue: Preview sink-mismatch: the design has VariableTemplateRenderer.render escape substituted values for the TELEGRAM sink (HTML-entity set for parse_mode=HTML, backslash set for MarkdownV2, and NO escaping at all for parse_mode=None). The preview endpoint returns that same string in PreviewStepResponse.rendered, which the new greenfield FunnelMessagePreview.vue renders in the browser DOM. Telegram-escaping is not browser-safe (e.g. MarkdownV2 backslash-escaping leaves '<script>' intact; parse_mode=None passes raw subscriber/custom-field values through untouched). The tech-spec's A03 rationale (Decision 9 / Risk row 'escaping drift') only argues the backend reproduces Telegram runtime escaping byte-for-byte; it never states the panel must avoid v-html. If the preview component uses v-html / innerHTML on the rendered string, it is a stored-XSS vector (author or, in the linked-bot case, a real subscriber's first_name/last_name/username/custom fields execute as markup in the author's browser).
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit constraint to the preview task (Task 6) and Decision 9: FunnelMessagePreview.vue MUST render the backend-returned string as TEXT only (mustache interpolation / textContent), NEVER v-html/innerHTML. If a visual approximation of Telegram HTML/MarkdownV2 formatting is desired, render the formatting client-side from a safe model or sanitize with DOMPurify with a strict allowlist before any v-html. Mitigating factor: the existing codebase has zero v-html usages and FunnelStepForm.vue already documents 'never v-html' for author text, so the safe default is likely — but this preview shows the RENDERED (substituted) output, a new sink, so make it a non-negotiable, test-asserted requirement rather than an implicit convention.

findings.issue: Test-run direct-enroll bypasses trigger matching by design (insertExecution depth=0). Verified there is no cross-tenant authz hole: the endpoint routes through requireFunnel -> requireOwned(ownerId, projectId) FIRST, then proves the funnel belongs to THIS project; projectId/telegramBotId used for SubscriberService.findByChat are taken from that already-owned funnel/bot context (not request body), and ownerChatId is read from the project's own Bot. A user therefore cannot test-run another project's funnel nor enroll an arbitrary chat. Residual (accepted, low) concern: the recipient is Bot.ownerChatId, set by Epic-04b 'first private /start wins' — a documented trust-model race where a non-owner could have claimed ownerChatId. Test-run/preview blindly send to / render data for whatever chat that is, so a hijacked ownerChatId leaks the author's preview data (subscriber PII) or delivers a test funnel to the wrong Telegram account.
findings.recommendation: No change required for this feature — accept the inherited 04b trust model as the specs state (Risk row + Decision 1). Track hardening of the 04b ownerChatId-claim race separately. Ensure preview/test-run never expand the blast radius by resolving any chat other than the project's own Bot.ownerChatId (the current design correctly does not).

findings.issue: Sensitive-data exposure check (ownerChatId / Telegram identity / bot token): PASS. Duplicate returns the existing FunnelResponse record, which carries only funnel metadata + steps + deepLink and NO ownerChatId/telegramBotId/token. Test-run returns a bare 2xx (enroll registered) with no identity payload. Preview's planned PreviewStepResponse is {rendered, sampleData, kind} — it must NOT add ownerChatId, chatId, telegramBotId, or raw subscriber identifiers. The rendered string itself does surface the linked subscriber's first_name/last_name/username/custom values, but that is the author's own linked account viewing their own preview, which is within the intended trust boundary.
findings.recommendation: Lock down the preview DTO at decomposition time: PreviewStepResponse must expose ONLY {rendered, sampleData, kind}. Do not add chatId/telegramBotId/ownerChatId. Add a unit/IT assertion that the test-run and preview JSON bodies contain no ownerChatId/token fields (regression guard against future DTO drift).

findings.issue: Stop-all is a bulk destructive operation (mass-cancel of all in-flight executions for a funnel) and test-run enrolls a real execution that triggers a real Telegram send. The tech-spec defines correctness/race semantics (claim-CAS, stepRunStatus=done) but does not mention an audit log entry for these privileged author actions. No security audit trail is specified for who cancelled N executions or who triggered a test-run send.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether the existing funnel module already emits audit/domain events on cancel (FunnelService.delete mirror). If an audit convention exists, have stopAllExecutions and testRun emit the equivalent (actor ownerId, projectId, funnelId, modifiedCount). If no audit convention exists project-wide, this is consistent with the current baseline and can be deferred — but note it explicitly so it is a conscious decision, not an omission.

notes: Design-level OWASP review of 13-funnels-tooling (4 new POST endpoints). Verified against actual source, not just the spec. STRONG points: (1) Anti-IDOR is sound — every endpoint funnels through FunnelService.requireFunnel, which calls ProjectService.requireOwned FIRST and then enforces funnel-belongs-to-project, collapsing cross-project/missing/malformed-id into a uniform 404 with no existence leak; ownerId is always from the session (currentUserId), never the request body. (2) Test-run direct-enroll has NO cross-tenant hole: projectId/telegramBotId/ownerChatId all derive from the owned funnel/bot, and findByChat is project-scoped. (3) Stop-all is scoped by projectId+funnelId (fail-closed tenant isolation, mirrors cancelActiveFor). (4) CSRF: confirmed in SecurityConfig — the @Order(2) session chain enforces CSRF on /api/** mutating verbs via CookieCsrfTokenRepository + CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler; the 4 new POSTs sit under /api/v1/... so they are covered with no extra work (FunnelControllerIT already uses csrf()). The integrations/api-key STATELESS chain that disables CSRF is path-matched to /api/integrations/** only and does not touch these endpoints. (5) No secrets/tokens in any planned response DTO. (6) VariableTemplateRenderer escaping for the Telegram sink is robust (HTML &<>" and full MarkdownV2 special set, single-pass backslash-safe). The ONLY actionable item is the medium A03 finding: the backend renderer escapes for Telegram, NOT for the browser DOM, and parse_mode=None does no escaping at all — so the new preview panel must render the result as text (no v-html). Codebase precedent (zero v-html, explicit 'never v-html' note in FunnelStepForm.vue) makes the safe path likely, but because the preview shows RENDERED substituted output (a new sink), it should be a test-asserted hard requirement. Verdict PASS: zero critical/high findings; the medium A03 item is a guardrail to bake into Task 6 rather than an architectural blocker.
